links.outcome: CRS reduction from human review queue prioritized by revenue risk versus random or confidence-based prioritization
links.effect: At 20% review rate, revenue-targeted prioritization achieved 43.2% CRS reduction vs 20.0% random and 19.7% confidence-based; 91% of oracle bound (47.4%). Simulation assumed perfect correction.
links.quote: At the practically relevant 20% review rate: S3 achieved F1-micro of 0.7423 with 43.2% CRS reduction; S3-TW (Tw-DRG targeting) achieved similar F1 of 0.7435 with 43.1% CRS reduction; while S2 (confidence-based) achieved only 19.7% and S1 (random) achieved 20.0% CRS reduction.

links.outcome: Generalizability of performance from single-center MIMIC-IV to broader US hospitals and Taiwan
links.effect: MIMIC-IV is a single tertiary center; DRG distribution differs from CMS national claims (top-20 concentration 23.9% vs 36.2%); Tw-DRG evaluated only by approximation (93.9% coverage); transfer to non-US systems should not be assumed.
links.quote: Institution-specific staffing patterns, documentation conventions, coding practices, billing resources, and technology infrastructure further limit generalizability to broader US hospital settings, and transfer to non-US healthcare systems (including Taiwan) should not be assumed from this dataset alone.

links.outcome: Zero-shot open-source LLM ICD-10-CM coding accuracy on 200 admissions
links.effect: Zero-shot LLMs performed far worse than fine-tuned models: MedGemma F1-micro 0.0185, BioMistral 0.0058, TachyHealth 0.0013, versus PLM-ICD 0.5934.
links.quote: The three zero-shot LLMs fared far worse: MedGemma (F1-micro = 0.0185), BioMistral (0.0058), and TachyHealth (0.0013), consistent with prior findings that task-specific fine-tuning remains necessary for ICD coding 20 .

links.outcome: Robustness of human review benefit to reviewer error (failure to correct AI errors)
links.effect: At 20% review, S3 CRS reduction fell from 43.2% (e=0%) to 38.9%, 34.6%, 30.2% at e=10%, 20%, 30%; still 1.5-fold greater than random at perfect correction. Simulated, not real reviewers.
links.quote: Even at the highest reviewer error rate (30%), revenue-targeted review retained 30.2% CRS reduction under MS-DRG, still 1.5-fold greater than random sampling at perfect correction (20.0%).

links.outcome: Model selection by accuracy and reimbursement risk
links.quote: Model CRS rankings mirrored F1-micro rankings (Table 3 ): PLM-ICD had the lowest mean CRS (24.86 per admission) and CNN the highest (31.45), a 26.5% gap in aggregate reimbursement risk.

Uniformly high AUC-micro scores (0.976–0.993) coexist with a wide F1-micro range (0.481–0.593): with 7942 codes per admission, the vast majority of code-admission pairs are true negatives that all models correctly identify.

links.effect: BioClinicalBERT F1-micro 0.4645 vs TF-IDF 0.5528; 99.7% exceeded 512 tokens.
links.quote: The self-trained TF-IDF baseline achieved F1-micro of 0.5528 on the restricted top-50 label space, while BioClinicalBERT reached only 0.4645, underperforming the simpler baseline because its 512-token limit discards most of each discharge summary (99.7% exceeded this length).
